Scope rewritten 2026-07-30. The original body and its QA report were written against an Angular 13 / @angular-eslint@13.5.0 / .eslintrc.json checkout. The repository has since moved to Angular 21.2.9 with ESLint 9 flat config, so neither the old acceptance criteria nor the old QA findings describe this codebase any more. Original acceptance ("update @angular-eslint/* to ^19.0.0") is met — the packages are at 19.8.1 and ng lint runs. What remains is that 19.8.1 is three majors behind Angular 21.

issues.display_title: Issue #407: Clean up stale ESLint flat-config for Angular 21
issues.main_description_html:
Clean up dead and incorrect configuration in eslint.config.mjs and the lint target in angular.json. All of it is stale relative to Angular 21 and typescript-eslint v8, and one item is a config bug that produces 42 false-positive errors.

Depends on #396 (the config rewrite lands there first).

Implemented in #412, stacked on #411.

Result

Before After
Total problems 673 641
Errors 75 41
Warnings 598 600
naming-convention errors 51 9

75 − 42 false positives + 8 newly covered = 41.

Tasks

1. Replace the removed createDefaultProgram option

eslint.config.mjs sets parserOptions.createDefaultProgram: true. That option was deprecated in typescript-eslint v6 and removed in v8, which this project is on. It is silently ignored today.

  • Remove createDefaultProgram: true
  • Replace project: ['tsconfig.json'] with projectService: true

2. Remove the prefer-standalone override

The config disables @angular-eslint/prefer-standalone with the comment "Project uses NgModule architecture (not standalone)". That comment is wrong:

  • grep -rl "@NgModule" src returns 0 files

  • src/main.ts bootstraps via bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, appConfig)

  • Components declare imports: [...] directly

  • Delete the '@angular-eslint/prefer-standalone': 'off' override and its comment

3. Fix the naming-convention filter regex

Of the 75 current lint errors, 51 are @typescript-eslint/naming-convention, and nearly all of them are kebab-case CSS design-token keys in object literals:

Object Literal Property name `bg-alternate-1` must match one of the following formats: camelCase, snake_case, UPPER_CASE
Object Literal Property name `text-3` must match one of the following formats: ...
Object Literal Property name `icon-color-2` must match one of the following formats: ...

The config already tries to allow these via its filter regex:

^(baseURL_GET|baseURL_go|CSGActions|[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)*|__.*__)$

The [a-z]+(-[a-z]+)* branch does not accept digits, so text-3 and bg-alternate-1 fall through and error. The identifiers are correct — they are CSS custom property names and must stay kebab-case. This is a config defect, not a code defect.

  • Widen the kebab-case branch to accept digits, or add an objectLiteralProperty selector with format: null
  • Verify the error count drops

Resolved — neither of the two options above was used. The regex already had one buggy escape hatch; widening it adds a second. format: null on a bare objectLiteralProperty selector would blanket-disable naming checks on every object property. Used the rule's own modifier instead:

{
  selector: ['objectLiteralProperty', 'typeProperty'],
  modifiers: ['requiresQuotes'],
  format: null,
},

Anything TypeScript forces you to quote is a wire format, not an identifier. Cleared 42 false positives, not the estimated 49.

4. Remove dead ignores, add real ones

  • ignores: ['projects/**/*'] — there is no projects/ directory in this repo. Dead.
  • Add dist and .angular so a bare npx eslint . does not walk build output. (Not hit today only because the builder passes explicit lintFilePatterns.)

5. Close the lint coverage gaps in angular.json

lintFilePatterns covers src/**/*.ts, src/**/*.html, api-modules/**/*.ts and misses:

  • server.ts
  • eslint.config.mjs — dropped deliberately

eslint.config.mjs is a .mjs file and tsconfig.json has no allowJs, so it is not in the TypeScript program. Adding it to the lint patterns while the **/*.ts block runs type-aware rules makes ESLint reject it with "file was not found by the project service". Covering it needs either projectService: { allowDefaultProject: ['eslint.config.mjs'] } or a dedicated non-type-aware config block — three-plus lines of config to lint one 120-line config file that the ESLint runtime already validates by executing it. Not worth the config surface.

server.ts was already in the tsconfig.json program, so type-aware linting works on it with no extra config.

6. Decide on max-len

'max-len': ['error', { code: 1000 }] is effectively the rule turned off.

  • Either set a real limit or delete the rule — do not leave it at 1000

Resolved — deleted. A real limit would mean a large reformat of the 6500-line main.service.ts, which belongs in its own issue if anyone wants it.

Acceptance

  • ng lint runs clean of all createDefaultProgram / dead-config warnings
  • @typescript-eslint/naming-convention error count drops from 51 to 9
  • ng build --configuration development still exits 0

The original acceptance criteria said "naming-convention <= 2" and "no more than ~26 errors total". Both estimates were wrong and have been corrected above:

  • naming-convention is 9, not 2. The estimate assumed only the two transferState parameter properties would survive. The real survivors are genuine findings: private methods missing their required leading underscore in elasticsearch.service.ts (2) and main.service.ts (1), an unquoted Authorization key at main.service.ts:6345, and 5 parameter properties across the two shared/translate/ loaders.
  • Total is 41, not ~26. The estimate did not account for server.ts entering lint coverage in task 5. It had never been linted and contributes 8 genuine errors — 4 require() imports and 4 unused Express handler args. New to the tracker, not regressions.

Both sets of remaining findings are #410's scope.

issues.display_title: Issue #408: Enable Angular template accessibility lint rules
issues.main_description_html:
Template linting ran with 3 rules. The 11 accessibility rules ship with @angular-eslint/eslint-plugin-template but were never enabled.

Depends on #396.

Implemented in #413, stacked on #412 → #411.

Result

Check Result
a11y rule violations found 2
a11y rule violations remaining 0
ng lint 641 problems (41 errors, 600 warnings) — unchanged, both findings fixed in the same PR
ng build --configuration development Exit 0

Original state

eslint.config.mjs spread only the recommended template config into the **/*.html block:

  • @angular-eslint/template/banana-in-box
  • @angular-eslint/template/eqeqeq
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-negated-async

The plugin also exposes an accessibility config that was not referenced anywhere. The Angular CLI's own generated ESLint config enables both. This gallery is a public-facing viewer, so a11y linting is not optional polish.

Rules this turned on

  • @angular-eslint/template/alt-text
  • @angular-eslint/template/click-events-have-key-events
  • @angular-eslint/template/elements-content
  • @angular-eslint/template/interactive-supports-focus
  • @angular-eslint/template/label-has-associated-control
  • @angular-eslint/template/mouse-events-have-key-events
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-autofocus
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-distracting-elements
  • @angular-eslint/template/role-has-required-aria
  • @angular-eslint/template/table-scope
  • @angular-eslint/template/valid-aria

Tasks

  • Add angular.configs.templateAccessibility to the **/*.html block in eslint.config.mjs
  • Run ng lint and record the new finding count
  • Fix the findings

Findings

Only 2, both empty anchors.

src/app/components/message/message.component.html:15 — <a href="javascript:;"></a>

No class, no handler, no content. Nothing in message.component.scss targets it. Dead markup, deleted.

src/app/villume-gallery/more-from-author/more-from-author.component.html:38 — .link-exhibition

.link-exhibition {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0; left: 0;
  width: 100%; height: 100%;
  z-index: 1;
}

A stretched overlay link covering the whole exhibition card, so it cannot carry visible text. Deleting it would break navigation. Given [attr.aria-label]="item.name" instead — the exhibition name is what a screen reader user needs, and elements-content accepts aria-label as an accessible name (confirmed in the rule source's safelist).

Note on the low finding count

The original issue predicted that interactive elements in the gallery viewer — artwork hotspots, navigation controls, dollhouse toggles — would be the bulk of click-events-have-key-events and interactive-supports-focus hits. That prediction was wrong. Both rules report zero, because every (click) handler in the codebase already sits on a <button>.

The low count is real, not a misconfiguration. Verified with:

npx eslint --print-config src/app/villume-gallery/villume-gallery.component.html

All 11 rules resolve to severity 2 on the largest template.

No rule was downgraded or disabled, so the acceptance criterion about documenting deliberate downgrades does not apply.

Follow-up worth raising separately

message.component.html:10 is an icon-only close link:

<a href="javascript:;" class="close-icon" (click)="showMessage=false"><i class="vi vi-x"></i></a>

No rule flags it — the <i> counts as content — but it has no accessible name, so a screen reader announces only "link". It also uses an anchor for what is a button action. Left alone here to keep #413 to what the rules actually report.

// update block:
ɵɵclassMap(ctx.colorTone);                          // binding merges on top

The static class is compiled into the element's const array and applied at creation; the binding compiles to a separate classMap call in the update block.

this.executeUpstairsFunction = true in main.service.ts — inside a function event handler this is the canvas element, so this wrote a property onto the DOM node. A repo-wide grep finds exactly one occurrence: the write itself. Nothing ever reads it.

Real defects fixed

no-async-promise-executor — 3 sites

The issue flagged this as the one to treat as a real bug rather than a style nit. Correct: a rejection thrown after the first await inside a Promise executor is swallowed.

  • setupSceneEnvironment → plain async method. The try/catch that only forwarded to reject is gone; throwing propagates naturally.
  • _focusOnArtworkAnimation → async method. It genuinely needs a Promise, because it settles from an animation-completion callback — but that wrapper now holds only the callback, and its executor is synchronous.
  • unselectAnimation → had no await in its outer executor at all; the await lives inside a nested setTimeout(async () => ...). Dropping async from the outer executor was the whole fix, zero behaviour change.

no-this-alias — 2 sites

The four BabylonJS keyboard handlers (_onKeyDown / _onKeyUp on two input plugins) became arrow functions, so this is lexically the plugin instance and both const THIS = this aliases disappeared. Safe because the dead executeUpstairsFunction write above was the only place a handler relied on this meaning the DOM element.

Remaining

no-case-declarations, no-prototype-builtins (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call), four no-empty-function, nine unused args prefixed with _, and the four template eqeqeq sites.

require() → import

server.ts and api-modules/ used require() because those packages ship no type declarations — converting naively produced TS7016. The change therefore comes with @types/cookie-parser, @types/compression, @types/cors, @types/body-parser, @types/request. The Express middleware is now genuinely typed instead of implicitly any.

Naming

  • getClientIPData / getContinentName / _FogEffectFourWall renamed to match the project convention.
  • Authorization exempted through the config's existing filter regex rather than renamed — renaming an HTTP header name would break the request.

Test fix, not in the original scope

not-subs-dialog.component.spec.ts imported async from @angular/core/testing, removed back in Angular 12. Switched to waitForAsync. ng build does not compile spec files, so this had been broken silently and only surfaced once tsc --noEmit entered the gate.

Not GitHub Actions. .githooks/pre-push runs ng lint, then tsc --noEmit. Wired via a prepare script that sets core.hooksPath on install — no husky, no new tooling dependency:

"prepare": "git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && git config core.hooksPath .githooks || true"

The typecheck step is not redundant. The untyped request import passed ng lint with exit 0 and failed only at build time — exactly the class of breakage a lint-only gate waves through. That is why the gate is two steps, not one.

Injected type error (import * as request) — ng lint alone exits 0 reject exit 1

594 warnings remain: 588 no-explicit-any, 6 prefer-for-of. Left at warn on purpose. Typing 588 sites is its own piece of work, not a merge gate. Worth a separate issue if the team wants it.

issues.display_title: Issue #416: Loading spinner never clears when a texture URL returns 404
issues.main_description_html:
Symptom

When a texture URL returns HTTP 404, the gallery's loading spinner never disappears. The viewer is stuck on the loading state permanently — no error, no timeout, no console rejection. Text walls are also affected: their textures can fail to appear with no diagnostic.

Root cause

Three separate promises in the texture-loading path can never settle. Any one of them is enough to hang the whole load. All three are on the same failure mode: an unhappy path that simply has no code attached to it.

A. fetchTextureFile rejection is dropped — this is the 404 path

main.service.ts:938

loadTexture(textureSource: any, forSceneEnv = false, scene: any = null) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const texureHasLoaded = () => resolve(texture);
    const failedToLoadTexture = (err: any) => reject(err);

    let texture: any = null;

    this.fetchTextureFile(textureSource).then((fileSource: any) => {
      // ... new BABYLON.Texture(fileSource, scene, ..., texureHasLoaded, failedToLoadTexture)
    });
  });
}

fetchTextureFile does reject correctly on an HTTP error — main.service.ts:1023, error: (err: any) => reject(err).

But loadTexture attaches only .then() to it. No .catch, no second argument, no reject forwarding. So when the HTTP request 404s:

  1. fetchTextureFile rejects.
  2. The .then callback never runs, so new BABYLON.Texture(...) is never constructed.
  3. failedToLoadTexture is therefore never wired to anything — it is defined, but only ever passed to a BABYLON.Texture that does not exist yet.
  4. The outer new Promise is never resolved or rejected. It stays pending forever.

The reject handler exists and looks like error handling, which is why this reads as safe. It only covers a decode failure after the bytes arrived. It does not cover the bytes never arriving.

B. utils.service.loadTexture has no error path at all

utils.service.ts:433

public loadTexture(url: string, scene: any): Promise<any> {
  return new Promise((resolve, _) => {
    const texture = new BABYLON.Texture(url, scene);
    texture.onLoadObservable.add(() => {
      resolve(texture);
    });
  });
}

The reject parameter is discarded (_). Only onLoadObservable is subscribed, and Babylon never fires that observable for a texture that failed to load. On 404 this promise is pending forever.

This is the one on the text wall path, and it is reached twice:

  • text-loader.service.ts:91 — _createTextMaterial, the initial text wall texture
  • text-loader.service.ts:53 — changeQuality, the quality upgrade

Note that the sibling implementation in main.service.ts (A above) does pass onError to the BABYLON.Texture constructor. Two implementations of the same job, one wires the error callback and one does not.

C. fetchTextureFile also hangs on an empty body

main.service.ts:1015

} else if (event instanceof HttpResponse) {
  const arrayBuffer: ArrayBuffer | null = event.body;
  if (arrayBuffer) {
    // ... resolve(blobUrl);
  }
}

If the response body is null or empty, the if is skipped, the observable completes, and nothing resolves or rejects. Pending forever. A 200 with an empty body hangs exactly like a 404 does.

Why the spinner never clears

villume-gallery.component.ts:846-894

this.mainService.scene.onReadyObservable.add(() => {
  this.mainService.loadExhibtion().then(async () => {
    // ...
    await this.loadAllArtwork();
    await this.loadAllText();

    if (this.mainService.ordinaryObjects.length != 0) {
      this.loadAllOrdinaryObject();
    } else {
      this.mainService.allAssetsHasLoaded = true;
    }
    // ...
  });
});

loadExhibtion awaits loadTexture for the lightmap at main.service.ts:5242 and for the scene environment at main.service.ts:5513. With defect A, that await never returns, so loadExhibtion() never settles and the entire .then block never runs.

allAssetsHasLoaded stays false, and the spinner is bound directly to it — villume-gallery.component.html:325:

@if (!mainService.allAssetsHasLoaded) {
  <div class="place-spinner">

There is also no .catch on this chain. So even after A, B and C are fixed so the promises reject properly, the spinner would still stay up forever — the rejection would just become an unhandled promise rejection. A rejecting promise and a pending promise look identical to the user here. Both need addressing.

The lightmap call at 5242 sits inside a try { } block, which is worth calling out: the try cannot help, because a promise that never settles never throws. The error handling that is present is unreachable, not wrong.

Reproduction

Not yet reproduced in a browser — this is a code trace, and should be confirmed against a live gallery before the fix is signed off.

Expected repro: point light_map (or any text wall picture_* field) at a URL that 404s, load the gallery, observe the spinner never clears and no error surfaces in the console.

Suggested direction

Not implemented — filing for triage first.

  1. Forward the rejection in main.service.loadTexture: give the fetchTextureFile(...) chain a .catch(failedToLoadTexture), or use .then(onOk, failedToLoadTexture).
  2. Give utils.service.loadTexture an error path — pass onError to the BABYLON.Texture constructor and call reject, matching what main.service.loadTexture already does. Consider deleting the duplicate entirely and routing text walls through the single implementation.
  3. Reject in fetchTextureFile when HttpResponse arrives with no body, instead of falling through.
  4. Add a .catch to the loadExhibtion().then(...) chain that clears the loading state and surfaces the failure, so a texture that genuinely cannot load degrades to a visible error rather than an infinite spinner.

Worth deciding as part of triage: should one missing texture be fatal to the whole gallery load, or should it be logged and skipped so the rest of the exhibition still renders? That choice determines whether the fix belongs at the loadTexture call sites or at the top-level catch.

Why the lint gate did not catch this

It cannot. ng lint and tsc --noEmit both pass on all of this — every promise is well typed and every branch is syntactically fine. The bug is entirely in the paths that have no code, which no static check can see.

Related: @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises would not have caught it either, since the promises here are awaited, not dropped.

Note — text walls are missing because of the backend data, not this bug

Verified against a live gallery (Y7S3x1ee) on 2026-07-31.

The API returns six text walls and none of them carry a picture field. The string "picture" does not appear anywhere in the viewer payload:

text_walls count: 6
[0] id=3ce3b0c4-c0f2-4eb5-b106-0822ce5c9d63 picture=undefined
    keys: color, content, deleted, font_family, font_size, font_style, id,
          line_height, name, position, rotation, scaling,
          text_horizontal_alignment, text_vertical_alignment

text.picture is therefore undefined, and _getTextsDataFromExhibitionData builds the URL from it anyway:

path passed to convertPathImage = "undefined?resize=50x50"
base64('local:///undefined')    = bG9jYWw6Ly8vdW5kZWZpbmVk
URL   = https://img2.villume.com/v/rs:fit:50:50:no:0/cb:.../bG9jYWw6Ly8vdW5kZWZpbmVk
curl  = 404

Confirmed by request, six times, one per wall. Artworks are unaffected because their image field is populated (.../446e84c50206b689.png?resize=1024x585), which is why paintings render and text walls do not.

A text wall is rendered purely from its pre-rendered picture — _createTextMaterial loads the texture and _createTextContentWrapper only builds an empty plane. There is no native text-rendering path, even though the payload carries every ingredient (content, font_family, font_size, color, line_height, alignment). The TextWall interface declares picture: string as non-optional, so TypeScript trusts a contract the API does not honour.

The frontend cannot fix this. The error handling described above only changes how it fails — from an infinite spinner into a clean skip. The text will stay invisible until either:

  1. the backend generates and returns picture for text walls, or
  2. the frontend renders text natively from content via BABYLON.DynamicTexture — a new feature, not a bug fix.

Worth splitting into a separate backend issue.

Context

Video artwork is no longer a supported feature. The editor stopped offering video upload in GoThruMedia/villume-admin#1756, and now shows a notice in place of the video instead of playing it (GoThruMedia/villume-admin#1758).

The gallery still played those videos, so a visitor saw a working video for a feature that is not supported and no longer maintained. This brings the gallery in line with the editor.

What changed

Video artworks no longer play in the gallery. The artwork canvas shows a plain notice instead:

Video artwork is not available at the moment.

  • Applies at both quality levels, so the visitor never sees a video — not while the low quality version is up, and not after the original quality swap.
  • The artwork keeps its frame, passepartout, position and size, and still behaves normally otherwise.
  • The artwork list still shows the real video thumbnail. Only the 3D canvas changes.

Machinery that existed purely to play video is gone: the play/pause controller that started and stopped playback based on camera distance, and the "Loading…" panel that appeared on the artwork while the video buffered.

Files touched:

  • src/app/shared/services/main.service.ts
  • src/app/shared/services/artwork-loader.service.ts
  • src/app/shared/services/artwork-loader-viewer.service.ts
  • src/app/villume-gallery/villume-gallery.component.ts
  • src/assets/img/video-unavailable.png (new)

One deliberate difference from the editor

The editor dropped its call to the external video service entirely. The gallery keeps it, because the same response also carries the thumbnail rendered in the artwork list. Only the stream part is dropped.

That also removes a hang risk on the same line the editor had: the stream was read off a find() result inside an RxJS next handler, so when no entry matched, the throw skipped the error handler and the promise never settled — closely related to #416.

Remaining / follow-up

  • video_stream on IArtwork is now written nowhere. Remove it once the editor side is settled.
  • Decide whether the artwork list should keep showing the video thumbnail long term, or also switch to the notice for consistency.

Verification

Type check, lint and build all pass. Still needs a manual check: open a published gallery containing a video artwork, confirm the notice appears on the canvas and the thumbnail still shows in the artwork list.
